# AMS purpose and first RSI loop

## Current understanding

AMS is a reusable system of workflows, rules, skills and tools for developing intent with AI and carrying it into verified outcomes. Its shared methods improve through evidence from actual work. The [Blueprint](../../BLUEPRINT.md) owns the final destination; [S-001 — AMS assessment](../specs/S-001-ams/SPEC.md) assesses a bounded build rather than defining AMS or parenting every Landmark. The [owner's purpose correction](#jot-37abcff9-7be7-49a9-9ddb-98e281445cc8) explains that distinction.

This room joins three kinds of work: building the public website, creating the RSI loop, and improving skills already used across projects. The website makes the system and its evidence understandable to visitors and to the owner returning later. Its own build supplies the first application of the loop; building a website alone proves no skill improvement. Other projects may later contribute evidence with their own versions, context and limits. [AMS website synthesis](design-concepts/landmark-ams-website.md) and [RSI presentation synthesis](design-concepts/landmark-rsi-presentation.md) distinguish explanation from measurement.

Shared skill improvements need no invented per-project delivery process. Substantial project adjustments, or adoption into an existing/new project, use `setup-workbench` in that project. Source merge, personal catalog installation and observed host loading remain separate facts. This page is a sufficient owner for AMS purpose; duplicating it in the Feature catalog would add competing maintenance.

## How the parts work together

The [local Grill Board](context-grilling-board.md) reduces owner coordination by preserving decisions and corrections through stable DQCs. Execution owners carry approved work through Landmarks, Specs and Tasks. The [RSI loop](context-feedback-improvement-loop-plan.md) uses failures and retained successes to compare bounded changes and decide what to keep; the [RSI Loop synthesis](design-concepts/landmark-rsi-loop.md) links its capability owners. Wiki maintenance turns resulting understanding into current, sourced explanations; it supplies neither execution authority nor proof that a method improved outcomes.

## Established meaning, limits and open work

The Blueprint and sourced owner clarification establish this destination and the website's explanatory role. They do not establish that the full autonomous loop, every website page or a broadly beneficial skill system has been delivered. Follow live Specs and evidence rather than reading the older preparations below as current state. In particular, the old statement that S-002 “owns the loop” is historical: LMK-004 owns the whole destination; S-002 owns evaluation and qualification. Stage A's exact RSI readback is now confirmed and its preparation delivered; Stage B implementation and existing campaigns retain their separate holds. # Governance core: the vocabulary explained

These words explain AMS claim roles, what binds an agent, how disagreements
between governing claims and the running system resolve, and the Workbench's
lanes, collections and decision records.

The [glossary](../../GLOSSARY.md#governance-core) owns the stack definitions;
the [Wiki schema](SCHEMA.md#governance-stack) owns their use in Wiki operations.
This article explains the model and preserves the owner's corrections. It
authorizes nothing. Later sections retain other Workbench explanations;
their terms are not all entries in the current AMS glossary.

## Governance Plane

Planes classify claims relative to a target and operation, not whole artifacts.
One artifact may contain claims on several planes or only one. For example,
a Spec can contain desired outcomes, learned rationale, supporting test results
and governing acceptance criteria; those claims retain different roles.

Definition: [GLOSSARY.md, Governance core](../../GLOSSARY.md#governance-core).

## Governance Stack

Always display the complete stack downward in the order below, or upward in
its exact reverse, keeping the plane numbers attached. The numbers describe
how Kayden uses the stack, not a ranking for resolving contradictory claims.

| Plane | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 6. [Projection](#projection) | Snapshot summaries of each plane's claims at the last visit. |
| 5. [Intent](#intent) | What the owner wants. |
| 4. [Enduring Context](#enduring-context) | What we know about what exists, Canon, Grounding, Intent and what to do with it. |
| 3. [Grounding](#grounding) | Evidence and proofs establishing and supporting the source of truth. |
| 2. [Canon](#canon) | The authoritative source of truth. |
| 1. [Actuality](#actuality) | What exists and is being worked on. |

### Projection

A Projection summarizes each plane's claims as of the last time we were
there. A Wiki overview, Board card or work summary can present these snapshots.
Keep source revisions or observation times visible; reading a summary does not
refresh its underlying claims or prove that they still describe current state.

### Intent

Intent is what the owner wants, with reasons, boundaries, corrections and
confirmation status. A Projection helps the owner develop or revise Intent.
Recording whether that Intent was delivered does not rewrite what was wanted
or create a new owner confirmation, acceptance judgment or Human QA receipt.

### Enduring Context

Enduring Context is our knowledge: what we know about what exists; what the
source of truth and evidence say exists or should change; and what we know
about Intent and what to do with it. It includes rationale, uncertainty and
lessons, not just historical reference. The name remains Enduring Context.
